chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was disobeyed with were six: love of the world, and love of leadership, and love of food, and love of sleep, and love of comfort, and love of women.'
ai.seo_question: What are the six things that caused the first disobedience to Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi identifies six primal desires—love of the world, leadership, food, sleep, comfort, and women—as the root causes of the first disobedience, linking human psychological tendencies to spiritual deviation. In Shia scholarship, these are often viewed as the 'corner-stones' of disbelief, illustrating how unchecked worldly attachments lead to the fall of Adam and subsequent human sinfulness. The narration emphasizes that these six loves are not inherently evil but become destructive when they become the primary focus of one's existence.
